llm1_reasoning: The conjecture's property P satisfies all three natural proofs criteria: (a) it is constructively computable in poly-time via the signal-processing transform, (b) it holds for 1/poly fraction of functions by design, and (c) it implies super-polynomial circuit lower bounds. This would yield an efficient distinguisher against strong PRGs, contradicting the existence of one-way functions under standard complexity assumptions.
llm2_reasoning: The conjecture explicitly satisfies all three natural proofs criteria: (a) the property P is poly-time computable from the truth table, (b) it holds for 1/poly fraction of functions (positive density), and (c) it implies super-polynomial circuit lower bounds. This would imply an efficient distinguisher against strong PRGs, contradicting the existence of one-way functions under standard assumptions.

conjecture.title: Truth-table discriminant for circuit hardness
conjecture.statement: There exists a poly-time-computable property P of 2^n-bit truth tables such that (i) P holds for at least 1/poly fraction of all functions, (ii) P(f) implies f requires super-polynomial circuit size over any basis.
conjecture.rationale: Define P via a signal-processing transform of the truth table.
